title: What even is dbt? An Analytics engineer explains | Laurie Merrell & Michael Chow | Data Science Lab
description:
The Data Science Lab is a live weekly call. Register at pos.it/dslab! Discord invites go out each week on lives calls. We'd love to have you! 

The Lab is an open, messy space for learning and asking questions. Think of it like pair coding with a friend or two. Learn something new, and share what you know to help others grow.

On this call, Libby Heeren is joined by Jarvis Innovations Lead Analytics Engineer Laurie Merrell and Posit Principal Software Engineer Michael Chow as they walk us through a beginner dbt project and let us ask as many questions as we like (and we do, we ask all the questions, including, WHAT EVEN IS dbt??). This is a super friendly, MESSY, collaborative, and curious peek at dbt. It's is a tool that's often mysterious to data scientists and it's a big enough framework that it can feel tough to get started with. Walking through the basics makes it way easier to get into!

Hosting crew from Posit: Libby Heeren, Isabella Velasquez

comments.text: What i learnt in this video is which framework i don't want to learn and use 😅
comments.author: @letstalkaboutmath2121

comments.text: I think Hadley had it right in the chat, he said that dbt solves a problem that is outside of his needs/experience, and it's the same for me! I'm glad I at least got exposure to it so I can talk more intelligently about that problem space :) I have been surprised, though, by how many people said that, as an analyst, they're also the de facto data engineer at their company.
comments.author: @Libby-at-Posit

comments.text: After watching the full video I still don't get what dbt is and why I should use it
comments.author: @jaywurst3784

comments.text: You aren't the only one! It was hard to wrap my brain around it! Hadley said the same thing 😂 He made a good point, that analytics engineering is too far from what a lot of analysts need to do everyday to land on us, but there were people in the chat who said they actually did have to do this stuff. I'm glad I got exposed to it, though.
comments.author: @Libby-at-Posit

comments.text: From what I can tell, "dbt" isn't actually defined in this video until 13:33, so go straight there if you need a definition, and then start the video over. Or, then go to 6:46 to get a little more context.

comments.text: Good lookin out, Jeff! There are timestamped chapters at the bottom if you open up the description box, too. I was really glad we were able to backtrack and define it before we got TOO much farther than that 😅
